name: Miami-Dade County School Board

meetings.pattern: Regular meetings about once a month, usually a Wednesday at 11:00 a.m., in the School Board Administration Building Auditorium, 1450 NE 2nd Avenue, Miami 33132. The public hearing for non-agenda topics follows the regular agenda and begins no later than about 6:30 p.m. Budget hearings are evening special meetings at 6:00 p.m. Workshops (budget, safety) are usually 10:00 a.m. The Board sets each year's schedule at its November Organization Meeting.

schedule.note: Organization Meeting (Tuesday): members elected Nov 3 are sworn in; Board elects Chair and Vice Chair; final approval of the 2027 meeting schedule

phases.name: Attendance boundary changes
phases.decides: First reading of school attendance zones for the coming school year at the April meeting (2026: conference session at 10:00 a.m. and initial reading April 22), with final action at a later meeting.

phases.name: Budget workshops
phases.decides: Two public workshops where the Superintendent and CFO walk the Board through the coming year's budget before anything is adopted (2026: May 20 and June 10 at 10:00 a.m.).

phases.name: Tentative budget and millage advertised
phases.decides: After the state certifies taxable values in mid-July, the Board at its July regular meeting authorizes advertising the proposed millage rates and tentative budget (2026: values certified July 17, advertising authorized July 22).

phases.name: First budget hearing: tentative adoption
phases.decides: Evening special meeting (6:00 p.m.) that tentatively adopts the millage levy and annual budget under ss. 200.065 and 1011.03, Florida Statutes (2026: July 29, 6.623 mills).

phases.name: Second budget hearing: final adoption
phases.decides: Final adoption of the millage levy, annual budget and related budget resolutions (2026: September 9, 6:00 p.m.).

phases.name: Instructional materials public hearing
phases.decides: Public hearing on textbook and instructional material adoptions (2026: September 16, 10:00 a.m.).

phases.name: General election (runoffs for Board seats)
phases.decides: Runoffs for School Board Districts 2, 4, 6 and 8 where no candidate won a majority in the August 18 primary.

phases.name: New terms begin, Organization Meeting
phases.decides: Members elected Nov 3 take office the second Tuesday after the general election; the Board elects its Chair and Vice Chair and gives final approval to the next year's meeting schedule.

phases.name: School fiscal year begins
phases.decides: The district's fiscal year (FY 2027-28) begins; the budget is operated on a tentative basis until final adoption in September. The July 1 date comes from state school finance law and was not stated on a district page fetched here.

levers.how: Speak on an agenda item: file a Request for Appearance (form FM-6314) with the Citizen Information Center by mail, in person, email (Request4Appearance@dadeschools.net) or the online form at cic.dadeschools.net, naming the meeting date and item numbers. Speakers are called in agenda order.
levers.rules: 2 minutes per speaker (or group spokesperson) per agenda item; 10 minutes total per speaker per meeting; a speaker not pre-registered needs a majority vote of the Board to be heard. Bylaw 0169.1.
levers.deadline: 4:30 p.m. the Monday before a regular Wednesday meeting (Tuesday if Monday is a district holiday); noon the last business day before a special meeting

levers.how: Speak on any topic not on the agenda at the Scheduled Public Hearing, which follows the regular agenda and starts no later than about 6:30 p.m. Register with the same Request for Appearance form, listing your topic.
levers.rules: 3 minutes per speaker regardless of number of topics; the hearing is capped at one and a half hours unless the Board votes to extend; large groups may pick a spokesperson; extra comments may be submitted in writing. Topics must relate to Board business.
levers.deadline: 4:30 p.m. the Monday before the meeting

levers.how: Budget hearings: register to speak at the July and September 6:00 p.m. budget hearings with a written request to the Superintendent (Room 102 or request4appearance@dadeschools.net).
levers.rules: Special-meeting deadline applies: noon the day before (2026 first hearing: by 12:00 p.m. Tuesday July 28).
levers.deadline: Noon the business day before the hearing

levers.how: Send written comments to the Board through the Citizen Information Center or to Request4Appearance@dadeschools.net; proposed policy changes have a written-comment period between first reading and final action (about four weeks), announced in the item.
levers.rules: Bylaw 0169.1 allows written comments when speaking time is not enough. Emails are public records.
levers.deadline: For policy changes, the written-comment date printed in the first-reading item

levers.how: Board office at the School Board Administration Building, 1450 NE 2nd Avenue, Miami 33132. Nine single-member districts; the Chair in 2026 is Mari Tere Rojas (District 6) and Vice Chair Monica Colucci (District 8).
levers.rules: Board office 305-995-1334; Citizen Information Center 305-995-1128; district main line 305-995-1000. Individual member emails are on the Board site (www3.dadeschools.net/SchoolBoard), which could not be fetched here.

levers.how: Ask the Citizen Information Center for district or Board records, verbally or in writing, in person, by phone, email (prr@dadeschools.net) or the online form. Requests may be anonymous and need no reason.
levers.rules: Acknowledged within 24 business hours; copies $0.15 per page; a special service charge and cost estimate if staff time exceeds 15 minutes; records are not released until payment. Student records go to the school principal.
No citizen initiative or referendum process exists for School Board policy. Changes come through the Board's policy process (first reading, written comments, final action).

The county charter recall process (Sec. 8.02) covers only the Mayor and County Commissioners. The Supervisor of Elections posts no recall procedure for School Board members; removal of a school board member is a matter of state law, not local petition.

levers.how: Run for the Board: qualify with the Miami-Dade Supervisor of Elections in June of the election year by paying the fee or filing petition signatures. Nonpartisan.
levers.rules: 2026: qualifying noon Monday June 8 to noon Friday June 12 (F.S. 105.031); fee $2,200.56 (4 percent of salary); or petition signatures equal to 1 percent of district voters, due noon May 11. Must live in the district by the day of taking office (F.S. 1001.361). Term limit: cannot run if you would have served 8 consecutive years by the end of the current term, counting only terms begun after Nov 8, 2022 (F.S. 1001.35).
levers.deadline: Noon on the last day of qualifying (June 12 in 2026; 2028 dates not yet posted)

levers.how: Board members are elected by district in the August primary of even years; if no one wins a majority, the top two meet in a runoff on the November general election ballot.
levers.rules: Even districts (2, 4, 6, 8) in 2026; odd districts (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) in 2028. Four-year terms starting the second Tuesday after the general election.
levers.deadline: Nov 3, 2026 runoffs; register 29 days before an election

elections.terms: Four years, staggered: Districts 2, 4, 6 and 8 elected in 2026 (terms end Nov 17, 2026), Districts 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 in 2028 (terms end Nov 21, 2028). Nonpartisan. Eight consecutive years limit under F.S. 1001.35, counting terms begun after Nov 8, 2022. District 1 has been vacant since Dr. Steve Gallon III resigned Aug 6, 2026.
